extracted.intended_audience: English/ESL teachers (particularly secondary/high-school) designing task-based classroom projects and teaching proposal-writing (health education/HIV-AIDS context)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running a task-based classroom workshop in which students brainstorm, draft, revise, and produce a formal project proposal (here: an HIV/AIDS awareness project) to build real‑world writing and project‑planning skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project stages / process
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal writing project included the following basic stages: (1) selecting a topic, (2) brainstorming, (3) pooling responses, (4) drafting, and (5) revising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sequence in a workshop format; allow individuals and groups to brainstorm, draft, revise until a final product is produced. Use iterative cycles of drafting and revision; teacher acts as facilitator throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic selection — relevance to students
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a topic that is highly relevant to students' day-to-day experience (e.g., HIV/AIDS, human rights, gender equality, democracy, health concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance motivates participation and authentic engagement; choose issues that deeply affect students to improve writing skills and civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop setting and logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify class level, venue, mode, sessions, and teacher role (example: 45 high-school seniors; District Resource Center venue; interactive workshop mode; five one-hour afternoon sessions during one week; teacher as facilitator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Off-classroom, real-world settings (e.g., resource center) enhance authenticity. Organize sessions to allow full student participation and to fit the chosen timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher role — facilitator and participant
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher is a facilitator of the project and ensures that the task stays learner-centered; the teacher may also participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate rather than dictate: support students' independent work, manage ground rules, model professional practices, and participate as appropriate to guide real‑life skill development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brainstorming ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and enforce collective ground rules to keep discussion on topic and avoid protracted arguments. Example rules: 'We shall listen to each other; All of us should take responsibility; Participation is voluntary; We will keep our agreements; Each of us should avoid hurting others; Mistakes are expected and one should not laugh at another; We should observe equality in our relationships.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ground rules (e.g., Brandes & Ginnis model) to encourage creativity, lateral thinking, respectful participation, and efficient use of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question framing for brainstorming
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions used in brainstorming should seek clear and basic definitions, explanations, and descriptions (e.g., 'What is HIV/AIDS? How is it transmitted? What should students do?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame questions that elicit factual, explanatory, and actionable responses to form the basis of proposal content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response generation, sorting, and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Students independently generate responses, then pool them; groups draw responses, evaluate and categorize them as 'good', 'better', or 'best', and select final items by vote. Eliminate misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gender-balanced groups; mix responses randomly (draw from a pot) to ensure fairness; use voting to reach consensus and teach critical evaluation (examples of eliminated misconceptions provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting, proofreading, editing, and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups organize selected responses into answers and a proposal through reading, drafting, proofreading, editing, and finally presenting a final draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize iterative revision and peer review; require presentation of polished drafts as a culminating activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and adaptation of model proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain a model project proposal (e.g., from UNICEF) and use it as a template; adapt and change details to match the students' written material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a real proposal model teaches format and conventions; students should adapt the model rather than copy it verbatim so the proposal reflects local context and student input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the problem and provide causes and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the issue matters locally and provide concrete contextual details to ground the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for the Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the proposed project is necessary to alleviate the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link the problem statement to the project's necessity; justify interventions with evidence or logical argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of the Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Give general details about how the project will address the problem, the timeframe of the project, and the expected results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear summary so readers understand scope, schedule, and expected impact at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Objectives and Goals (measurable outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the overall goal and specific objectives of the proposed project, including how the expected outcomes will be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make objectives specific and include measurable indicators for expected outcomes to enable monitoring and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Population (beneficiaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain who will be the primary and secondary beneficiaries of the project, including expected results for women and children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define target groups clearly and explicitly consider gender and age disaggregation (women and children) when specifying expected benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Participants / Collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all entities who will collaborate in the project with financial, technical, or non-financial contributions such as staff time and technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List partners, their roles, and types of contributions (financial, technical, in-kind); clarify responsibilities and collaboration mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Activities (logical sequence and roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the logical sequence of activities and how they will be accomplished within the given timeframe. Indicate the role of different communities and groups in the project, especially women and children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological activity plan, assign roles, link activities to objectives, and show community involvement and gender-sensitive roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability of the Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate how the project's impact will be sustained after the grant period is over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain plans for continued funding, capacity-building, local ownership, or revenue-generating activities to maintain impact post-grant (example: transition from well-wishers to member fees and sales of materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget estimates and alignment with activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the budget in local currency. Each budget line item must be clearly associated with specific activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a phase- or activity-linked budget, showing participant numbers, places, and costs; ensure transparency and traceability between costs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project organization and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Define organizational positions (example: Chairperson, Vice Chairperson, Publicity Secretary, Treasurer, Transport Officer, Committee Members) and democratic election procedures; ensure gender-sensitive leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify governance structure, election/appointment processes, eligibility criteria (example: Zambian teacher or student), and commitments to place women in leadership roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target group definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state the target group (example given: all teachers, students, and community members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about who benefits and how, to shape activities and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success / outcome indicators (project evaluation evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use indicators such as student attendance, teacher participation, dissemination of materials (e.g., resource center keeping a copy), and increased engagement (e.g., female students participating more) to gauge success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect qualitative and quantitative evidence (attendance records, stakeholder uptake, behavioral changes) to demonstrate project effectiveness.
